decision.note: The audit/remediation control plane is mature enough for normal use. Continue dogfooding and evidence-driven maintenance without displacing higher-priority product work.

strengths: GO mode is implemented as an evidence-backed Audit → classify → auto-fix → test → re-audit loop with owner-choice and external-blocked boundaries.
Public Pages generation performs live visibility checks and fails closed instead of trusting stale registry visibility.
Public Pages publishes public-repository details plus privacy-safe aggregate coverage only; private repository identities, URLs, SHAs, notes, evidence and findings are excluded.
Audit Coverage is now orthogonal to engineering CI: incomplete private credential coverage is preserved as PARTIAL rather than faked as PASS or misreported as a code failure.
Current public inventory and public-safe Todo publication are generated through the same validated Pages bundle.
Structured audits enforce nine independent evidence-backed quality dimensions and keep publication/IP gating separate from quality scoring.
A dedicated SECURITY.md now treats private-evidence leakage and publication-boundary bypasses as security issues.
The audited main baseline passed Portfolio Audit CI and the resulting GitHub Pages deployment completed successfully.

findings.title: The repository still has no explicit LICENSE
evidence: No LICENSE file is present at the audited commit.
The repository is currently public, so visible source code does not itself establish a clear reuse license.
findings.recommendation: Choose an explicit reuse license only when the owner is ready; do not infer MIT, Apache-2.0, or another license automatically.

findings.title: Actions credential does not currently provide complete private-repository coverage
evidence: The latest account scan observed 34 public repositories and 0 private repositories while the independently verified owner inventory is 43 total with 9 private.
The public aggregate coverage snapshot records audit_status=PARTIAL and does not expose any private repository identity.
findings.recommendation: Broaden or replace PORTFOLIO_AUDIT_TOKEN with a credential authorized for the intended private repositories. Until then, retain PARTIAL / external-blocked rather than claiming full-account coverage.

findings.title: Security reporting policy for private-evidence boundary failures was missing
evidence: SECURITY.md now defines private-evidence leakage, publication-boundary bypass, credential exposure and fail-open visibility behavior as security-sensitive.
The policy explicitly forbids putting private repository details or sensitive source material in public issues.
findings.recommendation: Keep the security policy aligned with future private-evidence and publication architecture changes.

findings.title: Private coverage failures previously made the engineering workflow red
evidence: Private-account scanning now records PASS/PARTIAL coverage separately from core engineering CI.
Incomplete credential coverage emits a warning and privacy-safe aggregate state while public bundle, schema, UI and deterministic audit checks remain independently blocking.
The main workflow completed successfully after this separation.
findings.recommendation: Do not downgrade missing evidence to PASS; preserve PARTIAL as an explicit coverage state.

findings.title: Public registry and Todo publication had drifted from live repository visibility
evidence: The public registry is synchronized to 34 current public repositories, including repo-auditor and we-read-template.
The generated Pages manifest reports 34 repositories, 8 public-safe Todos and zero live visibility exclusions.
Todo-to-Page synchronization is now part of the main Pages sync commit set.
findings.recommendation: Continue live visibility verification at build time; never treat registry visibility as authoritative by itself.

limitations: Complete private-repository audit coverage cannot be verified until the Actions credential is authorized for the intended private repositories.
Branch protection/ruleset administration was not evaluated.
The audit does not choose a software license or make legal/IP ownership determinations.
Static Visual UX checks are deterministic regression guards, not a full multi-browser visual test suite.
recheck_triggers: PORTFOLIO_AUDIT_TOKEN permissions or private-repository inventory changes.
Repository visibility, Pages publication architecture, or public/private bundle rules change.
Audit schema, quality dimensions, remediation classes, or GO execution policy change.
A LICENSE or external contribution/release policy is added.
New evidence collectors, language-specific adapters, or private evidence outputs are introduced.

reasons: repo-auditor is currently a public control-plane/tooling repository and no recorded confidential-input, employer/client/PI-request, patent-candidate, or ownership-uncertainty trigger requires it to be private.
The build pipeline excludes private repository identities and evidence from public Pages.
The missing LICENSE remains a reuse-policy owner choice rather than a confidentiality/publication blocker.

evidence: README, rubric, maturity model and policy clearly distinguish priority, quality, coverage, remediation and publication/IP gating.
The audited baseline passed Portfolio Audit CI including compilation, 43 deterministic tests, registry/schema validation, audit validation, freshness checks and JavaScript syntax validation.
Live visibility is fail-closed, private evidence is segregated, public bundle rules are tested, PARTIAL coverage preserves uncertainty, and SECURITY.md now documents boundary-failure reporting.

The observed Actions workflow uses an immutable checkout action SHA and the runtime is mostly standard-library tooling; broader dependency/provenance hardening is limited because repo-auditor is not a packaged release product.
Structured schemas, deterministic tests, exact audited SHAs, freshness semantics and reproducible Pages bundle generation make the control-plane behavior independently checkable.

Pages generation/deployment, generated-data synchronization and structured audit publication are automated; the repository still lacks an explicit LICENSE and formal packaged releases are not a current product goal.
README, POLICY, AGENTS, AUDIT_RUBRIC, AUDIT_MATURITY, SECURITY and the public workbench describe the operating model and safety boundaries.
Canonical public data sources, generated Pages snapshots, schema validation, Todo synchronization, freshness checks and regression tests reduce silent drift across the control plane.
The project has a public workbench and security policy, but no explicit LICENSE, CONTRIBUTING guide, code of conduct, citation metadata or formal release surface.
